items.title: Fed chair Warsh says price stability is key but shies away from signals about rates
items.summary: U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh says he won't prejudge what the U.S. central bank will do about interest rates at its upcoming meetings. However, he repeatedly vowed to “deliver price stability.” Warsh spoke Friday on the sidelines of a meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Bangkok. The global surge in prices is a key concern of the financial leaders meeting. Stubbornly high U.S. inflation is expected to lead the Fed to raise its key interest rate in coming months after a rate hike in September.

items.title: US Market: Fed's Goolsbee says latest US inflation data is discouraging
items.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee called the latest US consumer and producer inflation data discouraging, raising concerns about persistent price pressures. While temporary factors such as tariffs and geopolitical conflicts could ease, he warned that demand driven by the rapid expansion of AI data centres could require a policy response.

items.title: US Market: Fed Chair Warsh offers no signal on October interest-rate decision
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh gave no signal on whether the US central bank would change interest rates at its October 27-28 meeting, reiterating its commitment to price stability. Markets await further clues from economic data and policymakers on the rate outlook.
